title: 1. Hook: The Invisible Thief
text: Imagine you left a fresh piece of bread on the kitchen counter. A few days later, you find green, fuzzy patches growing on it. Who stole the freshness of the bread? You didn't see anyone!

title: 2. Socratic Thinking
text: Where do you think that green fuzz came from? Did it magically appear, or was something invisible already there, waiting for the right moment to grow?

content.title: 3. Discovery: Zooming into the Fuzz
content.description: If we use a magnifying glass on the bread, we see tiny stalk-like structures. These are living things too small to see with just our eyes!

title: 4. Reveal: The World of Microorganisms
text: Those tiny living things are called Microorganisms or Microbes. They are so small that they cannot be seen with the unaided eye. Some, like the bread mould, can be seen with a magnifying glass, while others need a microscope.

content.definition: A living organism that is too small to be seen with the naked eye.

content.question: Which instrument is typically used to observe microorganisms?

title: 6. Reflection
text: Explain to your friend why washing hands before eating is important, even if your hands 'look' perfectly clean.

title: 7. Connection
text: Think about the digestion process we learned before. Did you know our stomach and intestines contain millions of good microbes that help digest our food? Not all microbes are bad!

content.title: 8. Mastery: The Pond Water Safari
content.description: Take a few drops of water from a pond or a puddle. Place it on a glass slide and observe under a microscope (with your teacher's help). Draw the different shapes you see!

content.title: Teacher Tip
content.text: Remind students that 'micro' means small and 'organism' means living thing.

content.title: Common Mistake
content.text: Students often think all microorganisms cause diseases. Emphasize that many are beneficial (like yeast for baking, or bacteria in curd).
